source_text: Sanctum sanctorum est; in atrio comedatur. Non foris dogmata sancta spargere. Intra ecclesiam edere.
orientation: Origen is explaining the rule that the sin offering is most holy and must be eaten in the court, applying it to the church's teaching.
pass_a_gloss: It is holy of holies; let it be eaten in the court. Not to scatter holy teachings outside. To eat within the church.

choices.why: Renders the Hebrew superlative literally to preserve the ritual category of the sin offering as most holy.
rejected: It is the holy of holies

choices.english: let it be eaten in the court
choices.why: Keeps the passive jussive force of the Latin, matching the ritual command.
rejected: it is eaten in the court
one eats it in the court

choices.english: Not to scatter holy teachings outside
choices.why: Preserves the infinitive as a general prohibition, matching the abrupt homiletic style.
rejected: Do not scatter holy teachings outside
Holy teachings are not to be scattered outside

choices.why: Keeps the infinitive parallel to the previous clause and renders ecclesia with the glossary term.

bible_refs.note: Sanctum sanctorum est; in atrio comedatur

pass_b_english: It is holy of holies; let it be eaten in the court (Leviticus 6:26). Not to scatter holy teachings outside. To eat within the church.

last_rejected.why: Sanctum sanctorum = 'holy of holies' (superlative), not 'holy of holies' as predicate description. Better: 'It is most holy' or 'a most holy thing'.
last_rejected.fix: It is most holy; let it be eaten in the court.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Sanctum sanctorum' literally means 'holy of holies'; rendering is standard and meaning preserved.

last_rejected.quote: Not to scatter holy teachings outside
last_rejected.why: Missing subject/infinitive construction; 'est' or implied command lost. The Latin is elliptical but the English loses the grammatical force.
last_rejected.fix: Do not scatter holy teachings outside.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'Non foris...spargere' is infinitive; English 'Not to scatter' accurately mirrors the construction.
